title: Universal catenarity checked on minimal-prime quotients
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Then $A$ is universally catenary if and only if $A/\mathfrak p$ is universally catenary for every minimal prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-exc-excellent-ring]

proof.text: Assume $A$ is universally catenary. For each minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, apply [lem-per-universal-catenarity-quotient] to the ideal $I=\mathfrak p$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $A$ is Noetherian and universally catenary; it gives that $A/\mathfrak p$ is universally catenary.

source.place: Tag 00NK, lemma-quotient-catenary, second assertion; forward direction of Tag 0AUP, lemma-catenary-check-irreducible (2)

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $A/\mathfrak p$ is universally catenary for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. By [def-exc-excellent-ring], it suffices to prove that every finite type $A$-algebra $\varphi:A\to B$ is catenary. Fix primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak r$ of $B$. The contraction $\mathfrak a=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is prime: $1\notin\mathfrak a$, and $xy\in\mathfrak a$ implies $\varphi(x)\varphi(y)\in\mathfrak q$, hence $x\in\mathfrak a$ or $y\in\mathfrak a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] with $R=A$, $I=0$, and this prime $\mathfrak a$, obtaining a minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak a$.

source.place: Tag 0AUP, lemma-catenary-check-irreducible, prime-interval argument applied to a finite type algebra; Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology (4); Tag 00NL, definition-universally-catenary

proof.text: Put $J=\mathfrak pB$, the ideal generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak p)$, and $C=B/J$. Since $\varphi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q$ is an ideal, $J\subseteq\mathfrak q$. The map $a+\mathfrak p\mapsto\varphi(a)+J$ is well defined. Choose finite algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ over $A$ using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Their images generate $C$ over $A/\mathfrak p$: if $b=P(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ with coefficients in $A$, its class is the same polynomial in the classes of the $b_i$ with all coefficients reduced modulo $\mathfrak p$. Thus $C$ is a finite type $A/\mathfrak p$-algebra, so the hypothesis on $\mathfrak p$ and [def-exc-excellent-ring] imply that $C$ is catenary.

source.place: Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type (1); Tag 00NL, definition-universally-catenary; details supplying the omitted proof in Tag 0AUP (2)

proof.text: Let $\pi:B\to C=B/J$ be the quotient map. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], contraction is a bijection from primes of $C$ to primes of $B$ containing $J$, with inverse $\mathfrak s\mapsto\pi(\mathfrak s)$. Both maps preserve inclusion, since inverse image and image of subsets preserve inclusion. As inverse bijections they also reflect inclusion. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak q$, this restricts to inverse order-preserving bijections between the interval of primes $[\mathfrak q,\mathfrak r]$ in $B$ and $[\pi(\mathfrak q),\pi(\mathfrak r)]$ in $C$. Indeed, every prime in the former interval contains $J$, and the two inequalities defining either interval are preserved in both directions.

source.place: Tag 00E5, lemma-spec-closed; prime-interval argument of Tag 0AUP, lemma-catenary-check-irreducible

proof.text: Apply the interval bijection of the previous step to each member of a finite strict chain. Strictness is preserved because both maps are injective and order preserving, so the number of strict inclusions is unchanged. A prime can be inserted between two adjacent members precisely when its corresponding prime can be inserted between their images; thus saturation is preserved in both directions. As $C$ is catenary, [def-exc-excellent-ring] gives a finite bound on lengths in its specified interval and a common length for all saturated chains there. The same bound and equality therefore hold in $[\mathfrak q,\mathfrak r]$. The primes $\mathfrak q,\mathfrak r$ were arbitrary, so $B$ is catenary; and $B$ was an arbitrary finite type $A$-algebra, so $A$ is universally catenary. If an interval has equal endpoints, the corresponding chains have length zero; if $B$ has no primes the condition is vacuous.

source.place: Tags 00NI and 00NL, definition-catenary and definition-universally-catenary; completion of the omitted proof of Tag 0AUP (2)
